questions.q: Which formula is Ohm's law?
questions.explain: Voltage equals current times resistance.

questions.q: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows?
Two resistors of 100 Ω and 200 Ω are in series. Total resistance?
questions.explain: In series, resistances add: 100 + 200 = 300 Ω.

questions.q: Two 100 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. Total resistance?
questions.explain: Equal resistors in parallel: R ÷ 2 = 50 Ω.

questions.q: Why must an LED have a series resistor?
questions.explain: An LED needs current limiting to prevent excessive current and damage.

questions.q: A 5 V supply powers a red LED (2 V, 20 mA). Which resistor is needed?
In a parallel circuit, what is the same across every branch?
questions.explain: All parallel branches are connected to the same two points, so they have the same voltage.

questions.q: On a breadboard, which holes are connected in the main area?
options: The 5 holes in one short column
questions.explain: Each group of 5 holes (a–e or f–j) in a column is joined underneath.

questions.q: What is a short circuit?
options: A path with almost zero resistance, so huge current flows
questions.explain: With almost no resistance, I = V ÷ R becomes very large and components can overheat.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Electric current is measured in amperes (A).

questions.q: What is the SI unit of resistance?
questions.explain: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure voltage?
questions.explain: A voltmeter measures the potential difference between two points.

questions.q: How should an ammeter be connected in a circuit?
questions.explain: An ammeter is connected in series so the circuit current flows through it.

questions.q: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure a resistor's voltage?
questions.explain: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component.

questions.q: What does a capacitor store?
questions.explain: A capacitor stores electrical energy in an electric field.

questions.q: What is the unit of capacitance?
questions.explain: Capacitance is measured in farads (F).

questions.q: Which component allows current to flow mainly in one direction?
questions.explain: A diode conducts mainly in the forward direction and blocks reverse current under normal conditions.

questions.q: What happens when an LED is connected with reverse polarity?
questions.explain: An LED normally blocks current when reverse-biased.

questions.q: What is the main function of a transistor?
options: Act as a switch or amplifier
questions.explain: A transistor can control current and work as an electronic switch or amplifier.

questions.q: What is the function of a battery in a circuit?
questions.explain: A battery supplies electrical energy by maintaining a potential difference.

questions.q: A 10 Ω resistor carries 2 A current. What is the voltage?
A device operates at 12 V and draws 2 A. What is its power?
What happens to total resistance when more resistors are added in series?
questions.explain: Series resistances add together, increasing total resistance.

questions.q: What happens to total resistance when another resistor is added in parallel?
questions.explain: Adding another parallel path decreases the equivalent resistance.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a fuse?
questions.explain: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds its rated limit.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a switch?
questions.explain: A switch opens or closes a circuit to stop or allow current flow.

questions.q: What does an open circuit mean?
questions.explain: An open circuit has a broken path, so no current flows through that path.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a breadboard?
options: Build and test circuits without soldering
questions.explain: A breadboard allows temporary circuit connections without soldering.

questions.q: Which precaution should be taken before changing circuit connections?
questions.explain: Disconnecting the power supply helps prevent accidental short circuits and component damage.

questions.q: What is the function of a resistor in an electric circuit?
questions.explain: A resistor opposes current flow and can be used to control current and divide voltage.
